title: Bengaluru Police Recover Somaya's Stolen 1980 Olympic Gold and Seven Other Medals
excerpt: Two men have been arrested and all eight international medals stolen from the former India hockey captain's home have been recovered, along with valuables worth about Rs 3.5 lakh.
body:
• Bengaluru police have recovered all eight international medals stolen from former India hockey captain M. M. Somaya's home, including his 1980 Moscow Olympic gold medal.
  • Two men, Manikya alias Manikanta (31) and Bharat (25), were arrested on November 9 near Hagalahalli Cross in Ramanagara; they were remanded to eight days of police custody on November 10.
  • The medals had been stolen while Somaya and his family were in Kodagu; he discovered the burglary on October 28 and filed a complaint the same day.
  • Somaya, a three-time Olympian who captained India at the 1988 Seoul Games, said getting the medals back felt like winning the Olympic medal all over again.

Bengaluru police have recovered the 1980 Moscow Olympic gold medal and seven other international medals stolen from the Bengaluru home of former India hockey captain M. M. Somaya, arresting two men and returning the medals to the three-time Olympian. Somaya thanked the police at a briefing this week, saying the recovery felt like winning the medal again.

"I am extremely grateful to the Bangalore Police, who have worked really hard over the last few days. They have not been able to recover only the medal, but also some valuables stolen from my residence. I feel I have won the Olympic medal once again."

— M. M. Somaya, former India hockey captain, speaking to ANI

What was stolen, and what came back

The burglary took place while Somaya and his family were away in their native Kodagu district. According to the complaint filed on October 28, the family had left Bengaluru on October 25 and discovered the break-in when they returned. The stolen medals were the 1980 Moscow Olympic gold, a silver medal from the 1982 Asian Games in Delhi, a bronze from the 1986 Seoul Asian Games, a bronze from the 1982 Champions Trophy in Amsterdam and a gold from the Loiano tournament in Italy, along with participation medals from the 1984 Los Angeles and 1988 Seoul Olympics and a silver commemorative medal. The burglars also took valuables worth about Rs 3.5 lakh, including a 10-gram gold bangle, an 8-gram gold coin, two silver cups, six silver spoons, a silver pot and Rs 30,000 in cash, according to police.

Police said all the stolen medals and valuables have been recovered. A traditional Kodava dagger, a camera and an Olympic kit bag were also seized, along with the two-wheeler allegedly used in the crime.

How the case was cracked

The Indiranagar police registered the case and formed eight special teams under DCP East Dr Vikram and ACP Halasuru Balakrishna, with Inspector Anand leading the station team. Acting on information from informers, officers arrested Manikya alias Manikanta, 31, a labourer, and Bharat, 25, near Hagalahalli Cross in Ramanagara on November 9. Police said Manikya has 28 previous cases and six non-bailable warrants against him in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

Investigators said the gold and silver medals had been sold to a gold company in Rajajinagar and were recovered from there on November 10, while the remaining six medals and other articles were kept at a residence linked to one of the accused near Hoskote. The two men were produced before a court on November 10 and remanded to eight days of police custody. Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh announced a cash reward of Rs 1 lakh for the police team. Police said the break-in appeared to be a random selection and that the accused did not know the significance of the medals when they took them.

Why these medals matter

Somaya was part of the India team that won hockey gold at the 1980 Moscow Olympics, the country's most recent Olympic hockey title. He played at three Olympics and led India at the 1988 Seoul Games, and he also won Asian Games silver at Delhi in 1982 and bronze at Seoul in 1986. The medals recovered this week cover that whole arc, which is why the theft drew a citywide police response rather than a routine burglary investigation. Somaya said the police had been reassuring from the morning of October 28, when the theft was reported, and had spared no effort in cracking the case in a short period.
nri_angle: Somaya's 1980 Moscow gold is part of the sporting history diaspora hockey fans grew up on; its recovery closes a theft that reached from a Bengaluru home to India's last Olympic hockey title.
